newsitem.title: TAJIKISTAN: Russian troops kill four on Tajik-Afghan border.
newsitem.headline: Russian troops kill four on Tajik-Afghan border.

text.p: Russian border guards shot dead four people trying to cross the frontier from Tajikistan into Afghanistan, the Russian military said on Sunday.

The Russian border guards' press service in the Tajik capital Dushanbe said the incident took place late on Saturday near the Kalaikhumb border station, located on the Pyandzh River in the Pamir mountains.
"We were forced to shoot when our own forces came under fire from the Afghan side and we tried to stop them," a member of the press service said.
He was unable to identify the four and said there were no Russian casualties.
Russia deploys about 20,000 troops in the remote, mountainous republic bordering Afghanistan and China, where they carry out peacekeeping duties and guard the country's frontier.

There have been several such incidents in recent weeks along the Tajik-Afghan border. Drugs traffickers have taken advantage of instability in the former Soviet republic to smuggle narcotics produced in Pakistan and Afghanistan to Europe.

Fighters belonging to Tajikistan's armed Islamic opposition have also operated from bases inside Afghanistan although a ceasefire agreed in December has put a four-year civil war in the republic on hold.
